Question: Let \(f\) be a function defined on the set of positive rational numbers with the property that \(f(a\cdot b)=f(a)+f(b)\) for all positive rational numbers \(a\) and \(b.\) Suppose that \(f\) also has the property that \(f(p)=p\) for every prime number \(p.\) For which of the following numbers \(x\) is \(f(x) < 0?\)
Solution:
The rule turns multiplication into addition, so prime factorization determines the function. First \(f(1)=f(1)+f(1)\), giving \(f(1)=0\). Also \(0=f(u\cdot1/u)=f(u)+f(1/u)\), so reciprocals change the sign.

Repeated prime factors therefore add repeated copies of the prime. In particular, \(f(p^k)=kp\), and a denominator's contribution is subtracted. Evaluate the options:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(17/32)&=17-5\cdot2=7,\\
f(11/16)&=11-4\cdot2=3,\\
f(7/9)&=7-2\cdot3=1,\\
f(7/6)&=7-(2+3)=2,\\
f(25/11)&=2\cdot5-11=-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Only \(\boxed{25/11}\) has a negative value, so the answer is E. A product rule for a function often suggests factoring the inputs into primes.
